values.condition: Galactic total space velocity V_G from Table 2, calculated in the paper's Galactic velocity system using an LSR speed of 220 km/s and solar motion.

notes: HVS10 (J130744.34-004449.5): T:p11-b0 lists its only non-dash Monte-Carlo probability as P_unbound-Xue08 = 0.50 (the other potential-model entries are '—', meaning bound in those models), whereas T:p1-b6 and T:p13-b1 state that all candidates have unbound probabilities over 50%. HVS10 is retained because it is explicitly included among the final 19 candidates; the 0.50 entry appears to be a boundary/rounding discrepancy rather than an exclusion. No SDSS or Gaia source identifiers are supplied, so the identifiers recorded are the internal HVS number and the un-prefixed coordinate designation from Table 1 (T:p9-b0). US 708 is cited only as an introductory prior example (T:p2-b1), not analyzed in this paper, so it is not included.

HVS1: Target is HVS1 = J172524.12+565709.6. Table 2 reports R_G for HVS1 as 8.0±0.2(0.1) kpc; the parenthetical error is the one obtained with 0.125 dex adopted as the [Fe/H] error (T:p7-b6), so both reported errors are retained as separate values. The paper labels V_G as the Galactic total velocity; it is recorded here as the Galactic rest-frame total speed derived from its 6D phase-space calculation with the stated LSR and solar motion.

HVS2: For HVS2, Table 2 lists R_G = 7.5±0.9(0.3) kpc. The paper states that the bracketed Galactic-distance errors correspond to adopting a mean LAMOST [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6, T:p10-b1), so both the nominal and bracketed error variants are retained. No parallax value or explicit bound probability is reported for this star.

HVS3: Target star is HVS3 = J132422.30+312841.6. At T:p11-b0 (Table 3), the dashes for HVS3 in the Kenyon08 and Gnedin05 models indicate the candidate is bound in those models and that no unbound probability was calculated; I did not infer or record a probability for those cases. At T:p10-b1 (Table 2), R_G is listed as 9.0±1.5(0.5) kpc; per T:p7-b6 the parenthetical 0.5 kpc is an alternative Galactic-distance error when adopting the mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex, so both uncertainty treatments are recorded with the same central R_G value. R_G is interpreted as the galactocentric radius.

HVS4: Target star: HVS4 = J091255.48+140413.8 (Table 1, row 4; matched by identifier). No parallax is reported by the paper; the distance is derived from the photometric distance modulus. Two Galactic distance (R_G) results are given in Table 2 for HVS4 (10.1±0.9 and 10.1±0.3 in parentheses); the latter uses the mean external LAMOST [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6). In Table 3 (T:p11-b0) the '—' entries for HVS4 in the Kenyon08 and Gnedin05 columns indicate the candidate is bound in those potential models and no unbound probability was computed; per the paper's note (T:p11-b0 note b), no bound probabilities are quoted numerically. Table 2/Table 3 list escape velocities for HVS4 of 474 (Xue08), 519 (Pacyznski90), 551 (Koposov10), 574 (Kenyon08) and 590 (Gnedin05) km/s, which are potential-model quantities rather than the star's rest-frame speed.

HVS5: For HVS5, Table 3 reports unbound probabilities only for the Xue08 (0.57) and Paczynski90 (0.52) potentials; the dashes indicate the candidate is bound in the other potential models and no unbound probability was calculated (T:p11-b0). Table 2 gives R_G = 8.7 kpc with a parenthetical error 0.4 kpc computed using the mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex, in addition to the standard error 1.4 kpc (T:p7-b6, T:p10-b1). The V_G value is treated as the Galactic rest-frame total speed because it is the Galactic total velocity computed with the adopted LSR and solar motion (T:p5-b15, T:p10-b1).

HVS6: Target is HVS6 / J133115.50+150438.9. No parallax is reported. In Table 3, the entries for HVS6 in the Koposov10, Kenyon08, and Gnedin05 potential models are "—"; the table notes state that "—" means the candidate is bound in that potential model and that no unbound probability is calculated in that case, so no numerical bound probability is available. Table 2 lists R_G as 8.7±0.8(0.5); the text identifies the parenthetical values as Galactic-distance errors obtained after adopting a mean LAMOST external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex, so both error estimates are recorded with conditions.

HVS7: For HVS7, Table 3 lists an unbound probability only for the Xue08 potential; the dashes for Paczynski90, Koposov10, Kenyon08, and Gnedin05 mean the candidate is bound in those models, and no unbound probability is calculated (T:p11-b0; I:p11-b0). The bracketed 0.2 in the third column of Table 2 is an alternative Galactic-distance error derived when the mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex is adopted (T:p7-b6). No parallax is reported.

HVS8: For HVS8 (J113116.03+571131.1), Table 3 gives an unbound probability only for the Xue08 potential (0.54); the dashes under the other four potentials mean the candidate is bound in those models and no unbound probability is calculated (T:p11-b0). Table 2 lists R_G = 9.4±0.6(0.3) kpc; the bracketed 0.3 kpc error corresponds to adopting the mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6). No bound probability was reported as a numerical value.

HVS9: For HVS9 (J121811.06+284659.9), Table 3 (T:p11-b0) reports an unbound probability of 0.51 only for the Xue08 potential; the dashes for the other potentials indicate the candidate is bound in those models and no numerical unbound probability is calculated, so those dashes are not retained as values. Table 2 (T:p10-b1) gives R_G = 8.7±0.5(0.3); the two reported errors are retained as separate entries, the latter corresponding to the paper's adopted mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex discussed in Section 3.

HVS10: Target star HVS10 (J115209.12+120258.0). In Table 3, HVS10 has an unbound probability of 0.50 only for the Xue08 potential; the four dashes indicate it is bound in the other tested potentials and no unbound probability is calculated (T:p11-b0). The R_G value in Table 2 is given as 8.5±0.7(0.3) kpc; the parenthetical 0.3 kpc error corresponds to adopting the mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6). No parallax or explicit bound-probability value is reported.

HVS11: Target HVS11 is J004028.68+393853.0 (T:p9-b0, I:p9-b0). Table 2's R_G is labeled Galactic distance; its first error is the tabulated uncertainty and the parenthetical error is obtained when adopting the mean [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6, T:p10-b1, I:p10-b1). The paper reports unbound probabilities only; no bound probabilities are reported. No parallax value is reported.

HVS12: Target HVS12 (J171952.43+525035.6) identified via its designation in Table 1. Table 3 lists separate unbound probabilities for five Galactic potential models; all are recorded with their model condition. The paper does not report a parallax for this star. Table 2 gives two Galactic distance errors: 0.4 (default) and 0.1 in parentheses (recomputed with a mean [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex); both are retained as separate conditions. V_G is the Galactic total space velocity (galactic rest frame speed).

HVS13: Target HVS13 is row 13 (J063934.38+280912.8). No parallax or bound probability is reported for this star, so those quantities are omitted. Table 2 lists R_G as 13.5±2.3(0.7); both tabulated error estimates are retained, with the parenthetical error corresponding to the paper's adopted mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex. V_G is interpreted as the Galactic total space velocity in the Galactic rest frame as calculated by the paper.

HVS14: Table 2 reports R_G = 9.0±0.5(0.2) kpc for HVS14; the parenthetical 0.2 is recorded as a separate Galactic-distance uncertainty under the alternative [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6). Table 1 places HVS14 among HVS11-HVS19 with 'reliable' proper motions (T:p9-b0). The paper does not report a parallax or an explicit bound probability for this star. V_G is interpreted as the Galactic rest-frame total velocity, based on the paper's Galactic 3D velocity calculation using the LSR speed of 220 km/s and solar motion (T:p5-b15). Escape velocities in Table 2 are not among the requested quantities and were not extracted.

HVS15: Target HVS15 = J012947.93-021343.2, identified from Table 1 and Table 2 (row 15) of the paper. For the Gnedin05 potential model, Table 3 lists '—' for HVS15, which the notes define as meaning the candidate is bound in that potential; therefore no unbound probability (and hence no unbound_probability value) is reported for that model, and no unbound_probability of 0 corresponding value is extracted. No parallax is reported for this star. The Table 2 Galactic distance is listed as 8.9±0.4 with a bracketed (0.2) corresponding to the Galactic distance error obtained when adopting the mean LAMOST [Fe/H] external error of 0.125 dex (Section 3.1 text); both are recorded as separate galactocentric_radius results. V_G in Table 2 is the Galactic total space velocity computed with LSR motion 220 km/s plus the solar motion of (11.1, 12.24, 7.25) km/s.

HVS16: Target is HVS16 = J075303.30+272657.0. Table 2 at I:p10-b1 lists R_G = 12.7 +/- 1.7 (0.4) kpc; the text at T:p7-b6 states that the bracketed errors correspond to adopting a 0.125 dex [Fe/H] error, so both R_G error choices are retained as separate conditions. No parallax or directly reported bound probability is given.

HVS17: For HVS17 (= J142235.20+455631.3), Table 3 lists unbound probabilities only for the Xue08 and Paczynski90 potentials; dashes in the Koposov10, Kenyon08, and Gnedin05 columns mean the candidate is bound in those models and no unbound probability was calculated (T:p11-b0, T:p8-b5). The R_G entry in Table 2 is 8.5±0.6(0.3) kpc; the parenthetical 0.3 kpc is the error obtained when adopting the mean external [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6, T:p10-b1).

HVS18: Target identified as HVS18 = J130744.34-004449.5 (Table 1 designation), a candidate with 'reliable' proper motion (Table 1 notes). Table 1 lists its heliocentric radial velocity as 14±20 km/s and Table 2 lists d=6.1±2.6 kpc, R_G=8.4±2.6(0.8) kpc, V_G=527±140 km/s. In Table 3 (T:p11-b0) only Xue08 (0.53) and Paczynski90 (0.50) unbound probabilities are given for HVS18; the '—' entries mean the candidate is bound in those potentials and no unbound probability is computed (per Table 3 note b), so no values are recorded for Koposov10, Kenyon08 or Gnedin05. No parallax is reported for this star. Table 2 also lists escape velocities V_esc = 506, 526, 557, 609, 600 km/s (Xue08, Paczynski90, Koposov10, Kenyon08, Gnedin05); these are escape velocities, not velocity measurements of the star, so they are not recorded as a velocity quantity.

HVS19: For HVS19, Table 2 reports R_G = 8.3±0.1(0.04) kpc; the parenthetical distance error is from adopting a mean [Fe/H] error of 0.125 dex (T:p7-b6). Table 3 reports an unbound probability for HVS19 only in the Xue08 potential (0.63); the dashes for the other potentials mean the candidate is bound in those models and no unbound probability was calculated (T:p11-b0).
